failure_summary.description: Schema-optional parameters were placed in the required list, including a requested puzzle ID and word-length filter.
Requested searches or named-source news were omitted or not mapped to an endpoint that could provide them.
Some calls used a neighboring location field or a noncanonical selector or code value.

patch.reasoning: The schema-placement errors recur despite the general instruction to follow schemas, so the edit makes list construction explicit. The named-source omission shows a gap when a source is available only through a generic source-ID endpoint. Existing guidance already covers parameter meanings and canonical tokens, so those rules are not duplicated.

edits.target: - Use each endpoint's exact parameter names and required/optional placement. Bind every constraint only to the call it modifies; do not carry dates, limits, filters, or pagination across operations.
edits.content: - Use each endpoint's exact parameter names and required/optional placement. Build the required-parameter list from fields the schema marks required, and put schema-optional fields only in the optional list—even when the user explicitly requests them. A requested value does not make an optional parameter required. Bind every constraint only to the call it modifies; do not carry dates, limits, filters, or pagination across operations.

edits.target: - For overlapping endpoints, compare the exact input type and every requested output facet, not just the broad topic. If the user explicitly names a source or issuing authority, treat it as a constraint and prefer its matching endpoint over a different provider's similar result.
edits.content: - For a named publication or source, also consider generic endpoints that return content scoped by a source identifier, even if the source is not named in the endpoint title. Use the source's canonical identifier when it is documented or unambiguously known; do not omit the requested source merely because its endpoint is generic.
